text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Organisers of the Nordic skiing world championships in Trondheim are sad that Russian Lyubov Yegorova tested positive after her victory in Sunday's 5-km classic cross-country race. But they are happy that the doping test system is working. Yegorova was stripped of her world title.
-Kongsberg hospital will not perform operations on patients who refuse to accept blood transfers.
-It will become cheaper to crash your car now that the big insurance companies are competing harder for motorists.
-The strong crown and low interest rates pose a gift to workers and managers ahead of this spring's wage talks.

-A majority in parliament may want to introduce tougher measures against what legislators call greedy brokers than Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg is planning to propose. Under Stoltenberg's proposal, managers of insurance funds would have to commit themselves to keeping shares they buy for personal gains at least a year.
-Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland went to Lofoten in the Arctic North to learn about problems facing fishermen.
-The annual result of Aker Maritime shocked the Oslo Bourse and the share plunged.
